extra: Cover what makes an invoice legally usable as a record: the required elements, sequential numbering, and the difference between an invoice and a receipt.
Explain the elements a tax invoice generally must carry for a buyer to reclaim input tax, and say clearly that the exact list is set by each country. Do not name a rate.
The key point is that a proforma is NOT a demand for payment and does not create a tax point or a receivable. Contrast it with a quotation and a real invoice.
Explain when a credit note is correct versus a refund versus deleting an invoice, and why deleting a posted invoice breaks a numbering sequence.
Distinguish clearly from a credit note, including who issues which and in which direction the balance moves.
Cover the PO as a buyer-issued commitment and the three-way match against the goods receipt and the supplier invoice.
Cover the sales order as the seller-side mirror of the PO and its place between quotation and delivery note.
Cover proof of delivery, why it carries quantities but usually no prices, and the signed copy as evidence in a dispute.
Cover validity periods and the point at which a quotation becomes binding on acceptance. Contrast with an estimate.
The whole value of this page is the estimate versus quotation distinction: an estimate is an approximation, a quotation is a firm offer. Make that unmistakable.
Contrast an invoice (a request for payment) with a receipt (evidence payment happened).
Explain how it tells a supplier which invoices a lump-sum payment settles, and why its absence causes unallocated cash.
Distinguish an open-item statement from a balance-forward statement.
Cover common terms, early-settlement discounts, and how terms shape cash flow.
Explain the counting convention (from invoice date or from month end), and 2/10 net 30 style discount notation.
Cover sequential numbering, why gaps are a problem for an auditor, and prefix and series schemes.
Explain that an unearned retainer is a liability, not revenue, until the work is done.
Show a real balanced entry with debits and credits on the correct sides and equal totals.
Your worked example must actually balance, and you must say plainly that a balanced trial balance does not prove the books are correct.
State the accounting equation correctly and show one transaction hitting two accounts.
Use the SAME transaction as the cash-basis page so the two pages teach each other by contrast.
Use the SAME transaction as the accrual page so the two pages teach each other by contrast.
Your example must balance: assets equal liabilities plus equity.
Explain the three sections and why a profitable business can still run out of cash.
Cover timing differences: outstanding cheques, deposits in transit, bank charges not yet booked.
Cover the imprest system.
Distinguish a provision (an estimate) from a write-off (a specific decision).
Explain VAT as a tax on value added collected in stages, and be explicit that rates and thresholds are set by each country.

This page and the exempt-supply page are the most valuable pair in the glossary. The decisive point is that a zero-rated supplier CAN recover input VAT and an exempt supplier CANNOT. Make that the spine of the page.
This page and the zero-rated-supply page are a pair. The decisive point is that an exempt supplier CANNOT recover input VAT, so the tax becomes a real cost. Make that the spine of the page.
Explain that the buyer self-accounts for the tax, and why the entry is often net-nil for a fully taxable buyer but not for an exempt one.
Explain output minus input and the payable or refundable outcome. Never name a filing frequency or deadline for any country.
Explain structured formats and clearance versus post-audit models. You may name schemes as institutions but attach NO dates.
Cover the various national names for it and why it must appear on a tax invoice.
Explain the time of supply and why it decides which return period a transaction falls in.
Cover HS codes and the customs value as the basis. No country rates.
Formula: opening stock plus purchases minus closing stock. Worked example must reconcile.
Distinguish margin from markup explicitly, with the same numbers computed both ways.
Explain what it deliberately excludes, why that is useful, and the standard criticism of it.
Use the contribution-margin method and verify the arithmetic.
Tangible assets. Show straight-line with correct arithmetic and cross-reference amortisation.
Intangible assets, and note the separate loan-amortisation meaning. Cross-reference depreciation.

Show a real cost-layer walk: two purchase lots at different unit costs, a sale consuming part of both, and the resulting COGS and closing stock value, reconciling to the total purchase cost. Cross-reference weighted-average-cost.
Use the SAME two lots and the same sale as the FIFO page so the two pages teach each other by contrast. Verify the arithmetic.
Formula: average daily usage x lead time in days, plus safety stock.
Cover periodic versus cycle counting and what a variance means.
Freight, insurance, duty and clearing as cost components, and why omitting them understates COGS. No country duty rates.
